archetypes.name: Ivy / Prep
archetypes.oneLiner: Repp-stripe ties, oxford-cloth button-downs, and penny loafers borrowed from a 1960s New England quad.
archetypes.description: Rooted in mid-century collegiate style — tweed, madras, and the easy layering of a New England campus. It favors texture and pattern over shine, and it wears its history lightly rather than formally.

archetypes.name: Classic Tailored
archetypes.handle: A suit with somewhere to be
archetypes.oneLiner: A well-cut suit, a crisp shirt, and the quiet confidence of clothes built to hold a room.
archetypes.description: Built around the enduring logic of a well-made suit: clean lines, quality cloth, and details that don't shout. It's the look of someone who trusts tradition to do the talking.

archetypes.name: Workwear / Americana
archetypes.handle: Denim that's done a day's work
archetypes.oneLiner: Chore coats, selvedge denim, and boots that are meant to scuff — heritage utility worn proudly.
archetypes.description: Grounded in the clothes made for actual labor — canvas, denim, and leather chosen for how they age. It values function and durability as much as looks, and it wears its wear proudly.

archetypes.name: Rugged Outdoors
archetypes.oneLiner: Flannel, waxed canvas, and boots built for trailheads, dressed for the elements more than the room.
archetypes.description: Built for trailheads and cold mornings — flannel, wool, and waxed cotton chosen to handle weather first. It brings the outdoors into everyday dress without needing an actual mountain nearby.

archetypes.name: Minimalist
archetypes.oneLiner: Clean lines, a tonal palette, and nothing on the garment that doesn't need to be there.
archetypes.description: A pared-back palette and clean silhouettes, where the cut and the fabric do all the work. It finds interest in restraint — texture and proportion over pattern or logo.

archetypes.name: Streetwear
archetypes.oneLiner: Graphic tees, fresh sneakers, and drop-shoulder hoodies that turn the sidewalk into a runway.
archetypes.description: Born from skate parks, sneaker culture, and hip-hop — bold graphics, logos, and silhouettes built to be seen. It treats clothing as a form of self-expression as loud and specific as music taste.

archetypes.name: Mod
archetypes.oneLiner: Slim suits, skinny ties, and polka-dot precision borrowed from 1960s London scooter culture.
archetypes.description: A sharp, high-contrast look descended from 1960s London — narrow suits, clean geometry, and a taste for bold color against dark cloth. It's tailoring with a beat behind it.

archetypes.name: Techwear
archetypes.handle: Dressed for a city that's always raining
archetypes.oneLiner: Matte black shells, articulated cargos, and hardware built for a commute through the rain.
archetypes.description: Engineered fabrics and utilitarian hardware built for a modern, weatherproof city life. It treats a jacket like gear — waterproofing, pocket placement, and articulation matter as much as silhouette.
